features.description: A faulty userspace program exits without stopping the kernel or another program.
acceptance_steps: Launch a program that deliberately faults in ring 3
Observe a nonzero exit status and no kernel panic
Launch another userspace program successfully afterward
evidence: 2026-10-30: make fault-smoke booted the guest, logged in over serial, observed USER PROCESS FAULT pid=1 vector=6 and exit status -7, then observed /HELLO output and exit status 0.

features.description: A CPU-bound user program cannot prevent the kernel shell or another runnable process from making progress.
acceptance_steps: Launch a user program that loops without syscalls or yields
Observe the shell remain responsive and run another command
Terminate the looping program and run a new userspace program successfully
evidence: 2026-10-30: make preemption-smoke launched two CPU-bound /SPIN programs; both printed SPIN_READY, kernel shell answered uptime, and both were terminated by PID.

features.description: A user can start a background program, keep using the shell, and terminate the job by PID.
acceptance_steps: Run a long-lived userspace program with &
Run another shell command while it is active
Terminate it with kill and verify later programs still run
evidence: 2026-10-30: make preemption-smoke used run /SPIN & twice, executed uptime while both were active, and killed both jobs by distinct PID.

features.description: User programs can start, wait, exit, and be reaped without hangs or resource leaks.
acceptance_steps: Launch and wait for multiple programs, including a failed program
Verify the shell remains responsive and process slots are reusable
evidence: 2026-10-30: make fault-smoke observed failed child exit -7 and healthy child exit 0; make preemption-smoke launched 70 further /HELLO children, all exited 0, exceeding the 63 non-idle slots.

features.description: Normal interaction runs in userspace, with the kernel shell available for recovery.
acceptance_steps: Boot into a userspace shell
Run, interrupt, and exit user programs without losing input or output
evidence: 2026-10-30: make session-smoke boots directly into /SH and foreground /HELLO returns to the prompt; interrupting an active foreground child from that shell still needs signals or a terminal control path.

features.description: After login, /SH is the default foreground shell with bounded restart and kernel recovery fallback.
acceptance_steps: Login reaches the userspace prompt without manually running /SH
A nonzero shell exit restarts it, with a bounded failure limit
A clean exit or missing /SH reaches the kernel recovery prompt
evidence: 2026-10-30: make session-smoke launched /SH after login, rejected an overflowing exit code, ran /HELLO as a foreground child, restarted after exit 1, stopped after three failures, returned to recovery on exit 0, and fell back when /SH was removed from a temporary disk-image copy.

features.description: A userspace shell can pass a bounded argument vector to native ELF applications.
acceptance_steps: Launch the editor with a path argument without an interactive path prompt
Pass the maximum eight arguments to an app and reject a ninth
Keep the legacy one-path spawn and editor prompt working
evidence: 2026-10-30: make session-smoke launched /EDIT with /ARGS.TXT, verified /ARGS reported argc=8 and arg7=g, rejected a ninth element, and retained legacy /HELLO launch; make editor-smoke retained the interactive editor path.

features.description: Only the foreground process can read console input; background readers cannot steal keystrokes.
acceptance_steps: Launch an input-reading app in the foreground and read a line
Launch it in the background and observe a denied read
Return input to the shell after the foreground app exits
evidence: 2026-10-30: make session-smoke observed INPUT_OK foreground from a foreground child, INPUT_DENIED from a background child, and a responsive recovery shell afterward.

features.description: A userspace command can create or replace a text file and reopen the exact bytes after a normal guest reboot.
acceptance_steps: Create and replace a text file through the userspace shell
Reboot the guest without recreating its disk image
Read the replaced contents and compare exact on-disk bytes
evidence: 2026-10-30: make persistence-smoke saved and replaced /PERSIST.TXT from /SH, issued a guest reboot, launched a second QEMU guest on the same disk image, and read final version. Host mtype inspection showed exact bytes final version plus newline.

features.description: A failed userspace replacement on a full FAT16 disk leaves the previous file intact.
acceptance_steps: Fill the FAT16 disk until no free clusters remain
Attempt replacement from the userspace shell and editor
Verify both report failure and the exact original bytes remain
evidence: 2026-10-30: make save-failure-smoke filled the FAT16 data area, observed write and editor save errors, and compared /NOTE.TXT to exact original bytes after both attempts.

features.description: A user can edit a file, reboot, and reopen the same contents.
acceptance_steps: Create and edit a file through a userspace application
Reboot normally and verify exact contents
Exercise interrupted and invalid writes without corrupting unrelated files

features.description: A standalone userspace line editor can open, modify, save, and discard bounded text files.
acceptance_steps: Open a file, change text, save, and exit
Reopen the file after reboot and verify changes
evidence: 2026-10-30: make editor-smoke launched /EDIT from /SH in the foreground, inserted and deleted lines, refused a dirty quit, saved, discarded a later edit, reopened, saved again, rebooted with the same disk image, and compared exact host-visible bytes.

features.description: A documented UEFI x86_64 machine can boot, accept input, access storage, and shut down.
acceptance_steps: Boot on a named physical machine from install media
Exercise input, storage, application launch, and shutdown
Record supported devices and known limitations

features.description: An application can communicate over a documented network interface and protocol.
acceptance_steps: Configure a supported network device
Send and receive application data across a network
Recover from a disconnected or malformed peer

features.description: A userspace desktop provides reliable input, windows, and application switching.
acceptance_steps: Launch and switch between two applications
Use keyboard and pointer input without freezing the desktop
Recover the desktop after an application fault
